thread.title: Wall Street heaps praise on Broadcom in wake of solid 2Q earnings

title: Wall Street heaps praise on Broadcom in wake of solid 2Q earnings
text:
Download PDF version 10:26 08 Jun 2018 Reiterating his Buy rating and a US$330 price target, Craig-Hallum's Anthony Stoss expects Broadcom's second half of the year to be strong The chipmaker reported 2Q earnings that crushed the market's expectations
Wall Street analysts are heaping praise on the chipmaker Broadcom Ltd, calling it a ‘free cash flow machine’ and ‘one of the best risk-rewards’, after it whizzed past second-quarter consensus estimates on Thursday.
Reiterating a Buy rating and a $330 price target, Craig-Hallum’s Anthony Stoss is looking for a strong second half of the year for Broadcom , which he predicts will be driven by a rebound in their wireless business thanks to Apple ’s ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) next-generation iPhone. He also forecasts that Broadcom will go after mergers on a smaller scale, scarred by Qualcomm’s rejection of its offer, according to a note first obtained by the Fly, a business news site. READ: Broadcom announces US$12bln stock buyback, shares rise
Credit Suisse ’s John Pitzer, who is keeping his Outperform rating and a US$335 target, is just as bullish, noting Broadcom ’s expected 30% dividend hike in October as well as its recently-revealed US$12bn stock buyback.
The response to Broadcom's robust second-quarter performance has been mostly positive, but Tristan Gerra, a senior analyst with Baird Equity Research, is a tad more pessimistic on the chipmaker’s fortunes. Its “wireless revenue outlook for the quarter was weaker than we expected, with a seasonal rebound expectation in North America offset by weakness in Korea,” Gerra wrote in a note out today.
Still, Gerra expects a double-digit rebound in the company's wireless business to take place in the fiscal fourth quarter and is keeping a US$290 price target and an Outperform tag on the stock.
Thursday, Broadcom reported earnings per share of US$4.88, which trounced Wall Street’s consensus estimate of US$4.76. Its revenue for the quarter came to US$5.01bln, up from $4.2bn in the year-ago period. Broadcom expects its revenue in the third quarter to fall between US$4.97bn and $5.12bn.
Broadcom shares are down 3% to US$256.67 in early trade, dragged down by a report that the iPhone maker Apple , its key business partner, will produce fewer new cell phones this year than it did last year. Top stories
